Denver area students walk out of school in protest

From the AP: Hundreds of students walked out of classrooms around suburban Denver on Tuesday in protest over a conservative-led school board proposal to focus history education on topics that promote citizenship, patriotism and respect for authority, in a show of civil disobedience that the new standards would aim to downplay.

The youth protest involving six high schools in the state's second-largest school district follows a sick-out from teachers that shut down two high schools in the politically and economically diverse area that has become a key political battleground.

Student participants said their demonstration was organized by word of mouth and social media. Many waved American flags and carried signs, including messages that read "There is nothing more patriotic than protest."

While I'm theoretically in favor of promoting citizenship and patriotism for your country, I think it's also important to educate kids to respectfully always question authority and demand accountability from those whom rule over them. Brainwashing people into "Everything your government does for you is awesome!" is, obviously, dangerous.

I've never understood the reason people are so keen to encourage blind obedience to authority. Sure, it means more stability in the short term, but it's disastrous in the end. People are not and should not be expected to be good little soldiers/robots. I am also a bit sickened by the idea that pointing out flaws or wrongdoing is somehow unpatriotic. America (and pretty much every other country on the planet) has blood on it's hands, and to pretend otherwise is foolish, unproductive, and insulting. Pointing it out also does not diminish the good that America (and Americans) have done and are capable of, either.
